This interrogation is rhetorical (taqriri). The aim is not to seek information about something, but to inform of a reality: that it certainly was so. Yet the interrogative form was adopted so that man himself should ask about this reality and reflect that at one time he was not a thing worthy of mention, and now that he is a thing worthy of mention, he should have some awareness of the hand of divine power which brought him from non-existence into existence and from darkness into light, while he plays his role on the stage of this world.

In any case, through this interrogative and questioning form, several realities are indicated at this point. These are indications of a very high order. They are profound truths, and by keeping them in view, attention is drawn to points worthy of reflection.

One point is that you should pause and reflect on the time and circumstances before your coming into existence, at the beginning of your existence: that this world was just as it is, and man did not inhabit it. Reflect on how this world must have appeared at that time. Man is a creation of Allah, yet he regards himself as something great and is arrogant. But he does not consider that this world was as it is even in the ages before his own existence. Rather, the creation of this universe did not even expect the creation of man. But Allah willed it, and He created man.

Another point is that you should reflect on the moments in which this creature came into human existence. Concerning those moments, man keeps groping in the dark, whereas knowledge of the beginning of the creation of man can belong only to the Creator of the universe. Only the Creator knows how the addition of Hazrat Insan (Man) to this universe and this world took place. In the long history of this universe, it is Allah alone who has determined a specific role for man.

Another point is: how did the divine power bring this human being and set him upon this stage of the universe, and entrust to him a responsibility and a role? It prepared him for this. It wove the fabric of his role together with the lines of this entire universe, and provided for him those circumstances within which it would be possible and easy for him to perform the role entrusted to him. And after that, it provided facilities for him at every step. Thus this Hazrat Insan became bound up and interwoven with everything in this universe.

There are many indications and many points worthy of reflection which these verses present before the human heart, from which human thought and human reasoning derive lessons concerning the purpose of human existence, his intentions, and the system of his destiny at every stage from beginning to end.

These were the points concerning the beginning of man's creation. As for the system which was devised for the everlasting continuation of the human race and its perpetuation until the Day of Resurrection, that system is entirely different and has its own story.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 76, verse 2:

﴿Indeed, We created man from a mixed drop of sperm, that We may try him; and We made him hearing and seeing.﴾ (76:2)

Amshaj means "mixed." This refers to the state in which the male cell enters the female's ovum and mixes with it. It may also point to the hereditary characteristics of the male and female, which biologists call "genes." These are the traits that distinguish the human species from other living species, and through them the hereditary characteristics of the family are also transmitted to the child. The sperm then takes the form of a human embryo, and takes a form different from that of other animals. This mixed drop is the one to which the hereditary characteristics of the male and female are attributed; indeed, this mixed drop is the repository of many different hereditary characteristics.

Thus Allah created man from a mixed drop. He was not created by chance, nor is his creation purposeless and in vain. He has not been created as a plaything. Rather, man has been created as a responsible creature, for trial and testing. Allah knows well what that test is, what the examination is, and what its result will be. However, the drama that man performs on the stage of this world is only for the manifestation of the result, so that this result may be presented in an open court and reward and punishment may be determined upon it, and so that people may reach their good or bad end.

For this reason Allah made man hearing and seeing; that is, He gave him the means of perception, so that he may understand and know good and evil, may grasp well the reality of the actions and things of this world, and may pass this test well.

So the system that Allah determined for the continuation of human procreation and reproduction, and which He willed, is the system of creating him from a mixed drop, and in it there is profound wisdom and profound purpose. This is not a chance process devoid of thought. This wisdom and purpose is to test this human being. For this reason Allah placed within this being the capacity to receive guidance and to accept truth. Then knowledge, understanding, power and choice were bestowed upon him, and all these capacities, knowledge, perception, receiving guidance and training, were given to him by Allah in a precisely determined measure and quantity.

Then, along with knowledge, understanding and perception, He gave him the power and the choice to take the path of truth. Accordingly, having given him the ability to distinguish truth from falsehood, He left him free to take whichever path he wishes, whether he chooses the way of Allah or chooses some other way besides it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 76, verse 3:

"And We guided him to the way, whether he be grateful or ungrateful" (76:3). Here Allah describes the path of guidance as the gratitude for a favour. When guidance is bestowed upon someone, the first feeling that appears in the consciousness is gratitude; he knows that he was not a thing worthy of mention, and so Allah, by bestowing humanity upon him, made him a thing worthy of mention. Then He made him one who hears and sees, distinguishing him from other animals, and thus he became capable of knowledge and recognition. Then He gave him guidance through his nature (fitrah) and through the Prophets, and left him free: that by taking the path of guidance he might become grateful (shakur), or by taking the path of misguidance he might become ungrateful (kafur). The meaning of the word kafur includes that he goes to excess in ingratitude.

After these three attention-drawing pointers and admonitions, a person now perceives that he is a responsible and purposeful creature, that he is not free but bound around an axis and revolving around it. The capacities given to him are being reckoned, and this world is for him a house of trial. Here he has been placed as a test; he has not been put down on a playing field but seated in the hall of examination. In short, from these brief three verses there emerges a priceless treasure of thought and reflection, and the essence of lofty ideas, concepts and profound wisdom becomes manifest. As a consequence of all these points, a heavy responsibility is placed upon a person, and seriousness and dignity are attained in the maturity of consciousness and in conduct. These brief verses determine a person's outlook on life; they tell him the purpose of his existence and grant him awareness of life, and in their light a person determines his life and its values.

This is why, immediately after these verses, it is made clear what the outcome of this trial and test will be: what the result will be if a person takes the path of gratitude, and what the end will be if a person takes the path of disbelief and ingratitude.

The end of those who take the path of disbelief and ingratitude is given with great brevity. Why? Because the atmosphere and style of the whole surah are gentle and delicate, of ease, joys and the eternal blessings of Paradise. Therefore Allah does not wish to cloud the atmosphere of this surah by giving the details of the punishment of Hell. He says, with great brevity:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 76, verse 4:

"We have indeed prepared for those who reject faith chains, shackles and a blazing fire." The chains will be on their feet, the collars will be on their necks, and these people, bound in chains and fettered in shackles, will be cast into Hell. But after this brief mention, the address now turns swiftly, and with somewhat more detail, to the blessings of Paradise.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 76, verses 5–6:

﴿Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is camphor,﴾ and ﴿a spring from which the servants of Allah will drink, making it gush forth in abundance.﴾

This shows that the drink of the righteous will be mixed with camphor. It will be filled from a spring that has been made to flow especially for them, that is, it will be in abundance and plenty, like a river. It was the custom of the Arabs to mix camphor and also ginger (sonth) into wine, and in this way they tried to make wine more delicious. Here they are told that in Paradise too there will be a pure and clean drink, mixed with camphor, and this wine will be in very great abundance. Its standard will be such that it will be far more delicious than the wine of this world, and its pleasure will be so great that we cannot even imagine it. In truth, these terms are used to make things comprehensible, so that people may understand, otherwise the blessings of Paradise are in the unseen realm. We cannot form a true conception of them or interpret them correctly.

The people of Paradise are called al-Abrar in the first verse and ʿIbad Allah (the servants of Allah) in the second. This is merely to express nearness and love, and to proclaim grace and generosity: these servants of Allah will be near to Him. And their attributes and characteristics will be these:

This is a very clear and transparent image, and it is the portrait of those sincere and truthful people who fulfil the demands of Allah's commands and of the Islamic way of life. These people are exceedingly merciful towards Allah's servants, and they give preference to other servants of Allah over themselves. The fear and awe of Allah remain upon them, and they seek the pleasure of Allah. And in view of the heavy responsibilities that Islam places upon them, they fear the punishment of Allah at all times.

﴿يُوفُونَ بِالنَّذْرِ﴾ (76:7): "They fulfil their vows." That is, they honour the acts of worship and good deeds that they make obligatory upon themselves. They take the matter of the religion of Islam very seriously and discharge its responsibilities. They do not seek to evade these responsibilities, nor, after accepting a responsibility and taking an oath to it, do they neglect it. This is the meaning of their fulfilling vows. This is the sense of ﴿يُوفُونَ بِالنَّذْرِ﴾. Its meaning is broader than the jurisprudential and commonly understood sense of nazr (vow) and nazr-o-niyaz, and includes collective and religious responsibilities as well.

﴿وَيَخَافُونَ يَوْمًا كَانَ شَرُّهُ مُسْتَطِيرًا﴾ (76:7): "And they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread." The state and quality of that Day is firmly and well fixed in their minds: a calamity that will be general, and whose affliction will reach all sinners and wrongdoers. Therefore they fear lest they be caught up in the general and extensive evil of that Day. This is the condition of their stance and their God-consciousness (taqwa). They have a keen sense of this heavy responsibility and of the great obligations of religion, and they fear shortcomings and faults, even though they are worshippers and obedient to Allah.

The Qur'anic verse (76:8) reads: ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive﴾ — wait, I must translate the text faithfully; here it is.

"And they feed, out of love for Allah, the needy, the orphan, and the captive." This is an expression of their goodness, kindness and benevolence, but it is manifested in the form of feeding the poor and others. Despite the fact that they themselves have a great need for that food, since such people cannot be said to love this food unless they themselves are in need of it, yet despite this need they practise self-sacrifice and spend this food on others.

From this attribute it becomes known what the economic situation was in the polytheistic society existing in Makkah; there was no custom of generosity towards the destitute and the needy. For pride, boasting and show they would spend a great deal, but there was no sympathy for the poor. In this field of selfishness and miserliness, these righteous people, nurtured by Islam, were shady trees for the poor. Despite their own need, they would feed people. With the feelings of sincerity and love, and for the sake of Allah's pleasure, they performed this good deed. Thus their intention and their purpose are also shown here: how and why they spent.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 76, verses 9–10:

"We feed you only for the sake of Allah. We do not want from you any reward or thanks. We fear from our Lord a Day that is frowning and distressing, a long Day of hardship." This is, as it were, the waves of mercy and love within exalted hearts, and they are for the sole purpose of seeking Allah's pleasure. From these kindnesses they seek no recompense, not even thanks. They show no arrogance or pride, and they do not seek to establish dominance over the poor. They only wish that by this act they may be protected from the hardships of that severe Day, because charity averts calamity, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has informed the believers of this.

﴿Guard yourselves against the Fire, even with half a date.﴾ (Bukhari and Muslim)

The feeding of the needy was in truth an expression of the lofty sentiment these people held within themselves. In this way they met the basic needs of the destitute. However, the form in which help to the poor and needy is given can differ between societies, so it is not necessary that the form of feeding the poor and needy be the same as it was in the early period. The real matter is the sentiment that operates beneath the feeding of the needy. In every society, the wealthy should keep this alive, and their hearts should be sensitive in this matter. Feelings should be alive, and the spirit of goodness should surge within the heart; and under this spirit of goodness there should be no worldly purpose other than the pleasure of Allah, not even a worldly benefit, to the extent that even the expectation of thanks should not be before one.

In the modern era, organised taxes are imposed. Duties are placed upon people, and governments levy budgets for collective maintenance. Aid to the needy is also given. But the guidance that the Islamic system has given in these verses is fulfilled in only one aspect through these measures, and the obligation of zakat fulfils that aspect. But this is only one aspect, namely meeting the needs of the needy; whereas the Islamic system also aims that the givers too attain spiritual purity and rise to a high level. The refinement and training of those who help the needy cannot be neglected either. Just as some people regard the aid of the poor as a bad act, on the grounds that the poor are thereby humiliated and the givers' temperament is also corrupted.

The truth is that Islam is a creed of the heart; it is a system of training. If the spirit of giving is sound, then through it the giver is also reformed, and the poor also benefit. Thus giving brings two benefits, which this religion presents.

Here the announcement is made with great speed that these people will be protected from the evil of that day which they greatly feared, so that in the world too these people may be at peace, because here they take guidance from the Holy Qur'an and affirm it. Therefore there they will receive freshness and joy from Allah. They will not even perceive the day of severe calamity there, because here they used to fear and dreaded standing before Allah. Thus on the Day of Resurrection their hearts will be refreshed and their consciousness will be full of joy.

After this, further mention and details of the blessings of Paradise:

"And He will reward them, for their patience, with a Garden and silken garments." In this Paradise they will have a permanent dwelling, and they will wear silken garments.

The passage begins with the Qur'anic phrase "متکئین" and ends with "زمھریرا", which is the verse-span marker in the source text. The translation follows.

"Reclining there on couches" (﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ﴾), and the rest of the verse, ﴿لَا يَرَوْنَ فِيهَا شَمْسًا وَلَا زَمْهَرِيرًا﴾, meaning "they will see there neither sun nor bitter cold."

So their gatherings will continue there, in which they will sit at ease, and all of them will be prosperous and immersed in blessings and comforts, in pleasant climates, where there is neither the intensity of heat nor the freezing cold of winter. In any case, it is another world, in which there will be no sun or moon like those of our world. It will be a new world; this is all we can say.

Wa-dāniyatan ʿalayhim ẓilāluhā wa-dhullat quṭūfuhā tadhlīlā (Surah al-Insan 76:14): "And its shade will be near them, and its fruit-clusters will hang low, made easy to reach."

That its shade will be close to them, and that the fruits of the trees of Paradise will hang over them, bending low: what greater joy, delight and luxury could there be? This is the highest conception of prosperity and ease.

This is the general condition of that Paradise which Allah has prepared for His servants, for whom this description has been given, which is most beautiful and luminous, so that in the world they may read it in the Book of Allah and rejoice. The further details of these blessings and comforts:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 76, verses 15–19:

ویطاف ........................ سلسبیلا

These people will be in utmost ease and luxury. They will sit on couches in shade, and the shade will be deep and pleasant. In an excellent atmosphere, fruits will hang from the trees in such a way that they will be able to pick them whenever they wish. Then the drinks that are served to them will be in vessels of silver, and cups of glass will be circulating, and these glasses too will be of the white kind of silver. That is, silver will be made so transparent that it will appear as glass, the like of which does not exist in this world. Then the drink that is presented before them will be most suitable, according to the need of each person, and this drink will be brought from a flowing spring called Salsabil, and it will be extremely sweet and pleasant.

Now, as a further addition to their joy, those who will be serving them pure wine in silver vessels will be extremely beautiful youths who will always remain youths, and who will have radiant faces. They will not grow old as time passes. These people will always have faces fresh and beautiful like youths. They will appear as if they were pearls scattered about.

In a single glance, the Qur'an now presents the whole scene in very concise words and invites the reader to look upon it.

﴿And when you look there, you will see bliss and a great kingdom.﴾

Everywhere there will be nothing but blessings, and the equipment of a great dominion, in which the righteous (abrar) will live in luxury, those who are the near servants of Allah. This was the general state of Paradise.

Here, some particular things are also mentioned specifically, which are manifestations of this great governmental arrangement; as if they are a model of the governing system.

Upon them will be garments of fine green silk and brocade, and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them a pure drink.

Note: the passage you supplied is a partial verse-range excerpt, so the translation above reflects the verse text (Q 76:21) as quoted in the sentence fragment "علیھم ... طھورا". The commentary itself is translated below.

Sundus (sundus) refers to very fine silk, and istabraq (istabraq) refers to thick silk cloth. In circumstances where they are all adorned and living in great comfort, their Lord is providing these arrangements for them, He who is most generous and bountiful. And the value and worth of these arrangements increases further because they come from the Lord, may He be exalted. And at the occasion of these excellent arrangements, these words will also be spoken by Allah in their honour.

This passage is part of the commentary on Surah 76, verse 22, which reads: ﴿Indeed, this is a reward for you, and your effort has been appreciated.﴾

The speech from the higher realm is delivered in their honour, and because of these words the value of these bounties is doubled. With these words the details of the blessings of Paradise come to an end. Thus people are called upon: flee from captivity, chains and fire, and enter these blessings. There is still time, and both paths are open to you.

At the climax of this call to Paradise, and after the description of Paradise's pleasant blessings, the situation of these polytheists is now taken up. They are steeped in obstinacy and insist on denial, and they have not yet grasped the reality of the Islamic call. They wish to bargain with the Messenger ﷺ regarding the Islamic call, or they want him to abandon certain things he says that cause them great distress. On the one hand, these people bargain with the Prophet ﷺ, and on the other hand they persecute the believers. They inflict torment on them and prevent people from the path of Allah, while they themselves turn away from goodness, Paradise and the enduring bliss. In these circumstances, this final part of the surah comes, and the Qur'an comments on these issues in its distinctive manner.

انا نحن ................................ طویلا

[Qur'an 76:23-26 (ellipsis in the original): ﴿Indeed, it is We who have sent down to you the Qur'an in stages.﴾ ... ﴿and so be patient for the decree of your Lord and do not obey from among them a sinner or an ingrate. And mention the name of your Lord morning and evening. And prostrate to Him during part of the night and exalt Him through the long hours of the night.﴾]

In these four verses a great truth is stated concerning the da'wah (the call to Islam). This is a truth that should become firmly rooted in the lives of the callers to truth (du'at al-haqq), so that they remain in that state for a long time, reflect upon it, and try to understand its meaning well. They should fulfil its true meaning, its practical form, and its demands on faith and the soul.

The fundamental point of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)'s da'wah was the belief in Tawhid (the Oneness of Allah), and for a long period he presented it before the polytheists of Makkah. He did not present the belief in Tawhid before them merely as a creed. Had he only expressed a belief, it would have been easier for them to bear, because the belief in shirk (polytheism) to which those people were attached was not a firm creed with real strength and stability, such that they could use it to confront the belief in Tawhid. The Islamic belief in Tawhid was an extremely strong, simple and solid creed. The real matter is that certain circumstances arose with the Islamic da'wah and the Islamic belief in Tawhid, due to which these people rose up in hostility and enmity, and that historical struggle broke out which the Qur'an has also mentioned at many places. Because of the belief in shirk, the Quraysh in effect held a position of collective leadership. The network of supreme deities that had been woven around this belief, and then the collective interests that became attached to those deities, were the very things that caused the Quraysh to stand up against the da'wah of Islam. Yet their position was apparently entirely false, and with this false belief they rose up against the apparent, simple and strong creed of Islam. Moreover, the luxury, pursuit of pleasure, sensual indulgence and licentiousness of the jahili (pre-Islamic ignorant) life compelled them to oppose this new creed and system, because in this system there are legal and moral restraints, emphasis is placed on high human values, and restrictions are imposed on obscenity and unrestrained sensual indulgence, whereas they were living a life free of moral bonds.

These causes, whether they relate to collective leadership and dominance, or to power and interests, or to habits, common customs, traditions and inherited conventions, or to the freedom from moral limits and restraints, are what raised up the people of that time against the first da'wah of Islam. The same causes exist even today, and even today the da'wah of Islam in every country and every land is being opposed through these very causes and reasons. This opposition to the ideological da'wah is made for these same causes, and as a result the work of the da'wah of Islam becomes laborious, difficult and arduous.

Therefore, the callers to truth should reflect upon this truth for a long time and live within the realities stated in these verses, whatever the time and place in which these callers may be, because whatever the time and place of the Islamic da'wah, it will have to face the same conditions that confronted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) received a message from Allah that he should warn people of an evil end, and he was told:

﴿O you who wrap yourself up, arise and warn!﴾ (2:74) When he began the da'wah, these causes rose up against him. The entire nation stood up to block the path of the new call. They decided to keep the state in which they were established exactly as it was, although they knew that their creed was weak and could not stand. First a feeling of enmity arose within them, then they began to defend their weak and feeble beliefs. In defence of their collective condition, the customs of their life, the freedom and unrestraint they had, and the obscenity and vulgarity that prevailed, these people began to block the path of the Islamic da'wah, because this new call was a threat to them.

The confrontation with the Islamic da'wah begins in this way: at the beginning, a few fortunate souls respond to the call. They are subjected to torment, and through threats and torments an attempt is made to turn them away from this religion. After this, such propaganda is carried out against the da'wah that a false image of it settles in people's minds. All sorts of baseless accusations are levelled, so that if those who have entered have not desisted, others do not enter. This is because for those who have already understood the Islamic da'wah, it is easier to block new people than to stop and bring back those who have already been convinced.

After adopting these means, they began to put, in addition to threats and violence, all other kinds of pressure upon the Prophet (ﷺ), so that he would adopt a policy of give and take with them. They said that if he stopped speaking against their beliefs, their customs and their idols, they too would not interfere with him. This bargaining was exactly like the way people in worldly matters adopt a middle path for reconciliation. These are the very stages that confront every person who, at any time or place, carries out the work of the Islamic da'wah upon the manhaj al-nubuwwah (the methodology of Prophethood).

The Prophet (ﷺ) was indeed the Messenger of Allah. Allah protected him from trials and enemies. But nevertheless, the Prophet (ﷺ) knew that he was a human being and that his companions were weak, so Allah did not leave them to their enemies, and He gave them help, and at every step signposts were shown to them... Accordingly, in these verses there is mention of that help and of that guidance which was given in this difficult stage.

﴿Indeed, it is We who have sent down to you the Qur'an in stages.﴾ (76:23) 

This is the first point that deserves attention: it is shown what the source and origin of this da'wah is. This da'wah is from Allah and is for Allah, and Allah alone is its source. He has sent down the Qur'an. No one other than Allah has any part in it, and no call other than the call of Allah can join with it. Its guidance is taken from Allah alone. None of its thought is presented through any other means. It is Allah who has sent down the Noble Qur'an, and it is Allah who has commanded the Prophet (ﷺ). Therefore this da'wah is proceeding in accordance with the guidance of Allah and along the signposts that He has shown. For the source of this da'wah is the Qur'an, which was indeed sent down by Allah.

But falsehood is extremely arrogant and rebellious, and it often appears outwardly swollen, and therefore the believers are subjected to torment. Every kind of evil and trial lies in their path. The enemies of the Islamic da'wah can only do this: prevent people from accepting the Islamic da'wah, and persist in this. Moreover, they remain fixed upon their beliefs, customs and acts of mischief. In this era of evil, corruption and mischief, these people offer reconciliation and moderation, dividing matters into equal halves. This is an attractive offer in these difficult circumstances, and in such circumstances rejecting this kind of offer is no easy task. But in such circumstances a second admonition comes, and attention is drawn to this important matter.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 76, verse 24:

﴿So be patient for the command of your Lord, and do not obey from among them any sinner or ungrateful one.﴾ (76:24)

Because there can be no compromise between you and them. There is no bridge between you over which ideas and doctrines could pass back and forth, for there is a vast gulf between your method (manhaj) and the method of jahiliyyah (ignorance). Your conception of this universe differs from their conceptions. You are upon the truth and they are upon disbelief. You are upon faith and they are upon falsehood. You are upon light and they are in darkness. You are upon knowledge and recognition, and they are upon ignorance.

Then all affairs unfold in accordance with Allah's commands. It is the way of Allah's command and system that He gives falsehood an opportunity and respite, that He gives evil an opportunity, and that at times He keeps the people of faith in trials for a long while in order to purify and refine them. All these matters proceed in accordance with Allah's wisdom; Allah's decree and wisdom govern the world. Therefore:

﴿So be patient for the command of your Lord﴾ (76:24). Be patient until the time comes. Be patient under harm, be patient under hardships, and be patient even if falsehood prevails. Be patient even when the jugular veins swell with anger; you bear the truth. The Qur'an, which is based on truth, is with you, so hold firmly to the truth, be patient, and disregard their offers. These people want a decision according to a policy of give-and-take, and they want to impose their own words.

﴿And do not obey from among them any sinner or ungrateful one﴾ (76:24). Because these people do not want to let you worship Allah, obey Allah, and walk upon the truth. Because these people are wicked and disbelievers. They want you also to commit some measure of disbelief and polytheism, so that the matter may be settled on a fifty-fifty basis: some good things they accept, and some bad things you accept. In this way they wish to deceive you and win your consent. They fulfil your bodily desires; thus they offer you the position of leadership, and they also offer you wealth.

Utbah ibn Rabi'ah says to you: "Leave this affair, and I will give you my daughter in marriage. My daughters are the most beautiful girls of Quraysh." In short, in every age and every time and place, the callers to truth have been lured through these very means.

Be patient, even though you may have to struggle for a long period. Even though the persecution of Quraysh becomes severe and the path becomes long, patience is indeed a very difficult task, and it requires intense preparation and discipline, and that preparation is as follows.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 76, verses 25–26:

﴿And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening. And during the night, prostrate yourself before Him, and glorify Him through the long night.﴾ (25:76–26) This is the provision for the journey. Remembering Allah's name morning and evening, and glorifying Him through the long nights, keeps alive the connection with the source from which the Quran is being revealed, from which the call to Islam (da'wah) and the command to establish the Islamic movement (tahrik) have been issued. This same source is the source of strength, and it is also the source of the provisions needed for this path. The means of maintaining contact with it are dhikr (remembrance) and reflection, glorification (tasbih) and declaring Allah's oneness (tahlil), and supplication and worship, especially during the long hours of the night. This is because the path is long and the burden is heavy, so a very large provision is needed for it. In the solitude of the long nights, only the servant and the Lord meet in privacy, in an atmosphere of great hope and love. Through this meeting all weariness and all confusions are resolved, weakness and the lack of resources are removed, and all fatigue ends. A person sees that the purpose for which he is working is a great purpose, and in comparison to it, the struggle, the sacrifices, and the difficulties of the path appear very small.

Allah is Merciful and Generous. He made His servants responsible for the call (da'wah), revealed the Quran to them, and informed them of the weight of these responsibilities and the difficulties of the path. Therefore Allah did not leave His Prophet unsupported. He helped him, and this training and preparation to face the difficulties of the path is in reality Allah's help and support. This is the provision of those who work for the call and for the revival of Islam. In every age and every place, this call is one. Its method is also one, and its circumstances and events are also one. The people of falsehood (batil) have not always adopted one single way against it. The means that falsehood adopted against the Prophet (ﷺ) are the same that falsehood uses against every truth. Falsehood always comes against truth with the same kinds of means and resources. Therefore, the means and resources of truth must also be those that Allah has chosen.

What are the realities within which the advocates of truth should remain? These are the ones taught to the first caller, the Prophet (ﷺ). The first and foremost point is that this call is from Allah, and this work is Allah's work. The second point is that this truth, which has come from Allah, cannot be mixed with falsehood. Nor can there be mutual cooperation between the people of truth and the people of falsehood, or bargaining on the basis of "give some and take some," because the methods of the two are different and their paths are separate. If at some time falsehood prevails because of its power and dominance, then there is also the pleasure and wisdom of Allah in this. In such circumstances, patience is necessary for the believers, and there is wisdom of Allah in it. The people of truth are commanded to overcome difficulties through patience, prayer, glorification, declaration of Allah's oneness, and dhikr and reflection. This is the great reality that all those who rise up with the call of religion must fully comprehend.

After this, it is said that between the method of those people, which is the method of jahiliyyah (ignorance), and the Islamic method, which is the divine method (minhaj), there is complete separation and difference. These people do not want good for themselves; their aims and objectives are very base, and their thinking is very narrow. What is the difference between the two?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 76, verse 27:

"These people love the fleeting thing (this world) and neglect the heavy day that lies ahead of them."

These are people whose hopes are very near, who regard very small things as great and important, and whose thinking and demands are very petty. They are small people, lost in this world; the days and nights of this world alone matter to them. And that great and weighty day, the day of heavy responsibilities, is hidden from their sight, though it will certainly be a very heavy day. These are people whom no one can follow in any matter, and whose path no one can take. They never meet the believers at any crossroads, and they share no common aim with them on any point. Their eyes are fixed on this world, on its power and on its wealth and possessions, which are extremely worthless and of little value.

It is said that these people are heedless of the essential matter. They seize what is quickly obtained, and they forget the day of heavy consequences, when they will be seized in chains and shackles and a severe reckoning will take place.

In this verse, the address is directed to the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions, that these people are such, and that they should be treated accordingly. But indirectly it is also a warning to those who are worldly-minded and occupied with the arrangements of this world. Such worldly people, in reality, are of no use to the work of the Islamic movement.

Now it is stated that Allah Himself has granted them these circumstances: this power, this status, this grandeur, all have been given to them by Allah. Allah is able to make these people weak and feeble and to strip them of this condition. But the affairs of Allah are based on profound wisdom, and He has been running this world according to His wisdom for a long time.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 76, verse 28:

We created them and made firm their frame. (Quranic quotation, per instructions: "نحن خلقنھم .................... تبدیلا" is a verse fragment, so translate as given.)

Here is the translation of the passage:

نحن خلقنھم .................... تبدیلا

This is a warning and admonition to those who are proud of their own strength: that the true source of your power, and even of your very existence, is in reality Us. Then the believers are assured that although you are few and weak, the Being whose call you have taken up is a Being of supreme might. You also know that all events come into existence by the power of Allah, and that Allah's power operates behind them. All affairs are carried out in accordance with His wisdom, and He is Ahkam al-Hakimin (the Most Judicious of Judges).

واذا شئنا ................ تبدیلا (18:76) "And when We will, We can replace them with others like them." They cannot do anything against Allah. It is Allah who created them, and it is Allah who gave them their strength. He is capable of raising up another people against them to take their place. That He has so far granted them respite and has not raised another power in their place is Allah's grace and mercy, and is His decision and wisdom.

From this it is evident that in this verse too the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is being consoled, and his companions are being encouraged. The position of the people of faith and the position of others are being clarified, and those who are immersed in the affairs of this world, and who are proud of their strength, are being warned that they should appreciate the blessings of Allah, rather than making Allah's blessings a means of pride, instead of giving thanks, and should keep in mind that these blessings and this respite are in reality a trial, as was explicitly stated at the beginning of the surah.

After this, their attention is drawn to the fact that every moment of the respite granted to you is very precious for you. The Quran is the mercy of Allah. It is being revealed continuously, and this surah is also a reminder.

The verse is quoted as: ﴿Indeed, this is a reminder, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way.﴾ (Surah al-Insan 76:29), and the passage below is the Urdu commentary's continuation.

And after this, it is also made clear that Allah's will is unrestricted, and everything comes into being in accordance with Allah's will. So that people's final attention is directed towards Allah, and in the end all people bow in submission before Allah. Rather than being proud of their own strength, a person should rely upon the strength of Allah, and hold the belief that true power is in the hand of Allah, that is, bow completely before Allah.

This is so that human hearts may know that the true doer of choice is Allah. He alone is the one who disposes and exercises absolute control, so that all hearts turn towards Allah alone and bow their heads in submission before Him. This is the reality that these verses express: the ultimate doer of choice is Allah, yet Allah has given man the capacity to understand truth and falsehood, and to turn toward truth or falsehood in accordance with Allah's will. For this purpose Allah also granted man knowledge and recognition. And by sending Messengers, He explained clearly to mankind the path of truth and falsehood. And by sending down the Qur'an and other Scriptures, He also indicated the way. But all these matters lie within the sphere of Allah's power and will. Therefore, whoever turns his face toward Allah, Allah grants him the ability (tawfiq) to come onto the right path. When a person does not turn toward Allah and does not raise his hands in supplication before Him, he is deprived of guidance and success, and such a person is not granted tawfiq.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 76, verse 31:

Yudkhilu ............................ al-alima

In short, the will of Allah is unrestricted; He decides as He wishes. If Allah wills, He admits anyone He pleases into His mercy, from among mankind, whoever supplicates to enter His mercy. Seek Allah's help in obedience to Him, and seek the guidance that comes through divine grace, while for the wrongdoers He has prepared a punishment that is very painful, and Allah has granted them respite in this world so that they may arrive at the painful punishment.

The conclusion of the surah is in harmony with its beginning. In it, the final outcome of the trial is made known, for which Allah created man from a mingled drop of semen (nutfah amshaj) and for which Allah gave man hearing and sight, and showed him the way to Paradise and Hell.
